basis: Hereditary susceptibility to ovarian cancer; reproductive organs have no axis, and susceptibility does not establish organ damage.
Fibrosis directly affects the endocardium and atrioventricular valves, causing restrictive cardiomyopathy and valvular dysfunction.
Severe CNS hypomyelination defines disease. Nystagmus and muscle wasting reflect neurologic dysfunction; stridor alone does not establish airway damage; respiratory failure occurs in 5-29%.
Developmental impairment, hypotonia and ataxia define the neurologic disorder. Dysmorphic features and malocclusion in isolated patients do not establish common additional organ damage.
Neurodegeneration and blindness define the syndrome; blindness, seizures, spasticity and severe developmental impairment occur in 80-99%.
Neoplasm directly occupies the spinal cord; no additional organ damage applies across most subtypes.
Inclusion body myopathy and cerebral white matter abnormalities define disease. Ptosis in 4/11 reflects muscle dysfunction rather than independent ocular damage.
Disordered glycogen metabolism causes progressive myoclonic epilepsy and neurodegeneration. Visual seizures are neurologic; common damaging hepatic involvement is not established.
Carcinoma originates in the sublingual salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Progressive nephropathy and deafness are the defining renal and auditory manifestations.
